lessons.title: Designing a farm data collection plan
lessons.html:
Why collect data?

Decisions about fertiliser, irrigation, breeding, labour and marketing are only as good as the information behind them. A data collection plan ensures the right data are collected consistently, accurately and in a form that can be analysed. It also supports compliance with audits, food safety schemes, labour law and lenders.

Elements of a data collection plan

  1. Purpose: the question or decision the data must support, such as "Which maize cultivar gives the best gross margin on our soils?" or "Is our calving percentage improving?"
  2. Variables: exactly what will be measured, with units: yield in tonnes per hectare at a stated moisture, weaning mass in kg, water use in cubic metres.
  3. Method: how each variable is measured: weighbridge, scale, rain gauge, flow meter, field count, lab test.
  4. Sampling: where, how many and how often, such as five random 10 m row samples per block, or all calves weighed at weaning.
  5. Responsibility: who collects, checks and captures the data.
  6. Tools and forms: standard paper forms, spreadsheets, farm management software or mobile apps.
  7. Timing: schedule and deadlines.
  8. Storage, security and backup.
  9. Analysis and reporting: how and when the data will be summarised and to whom.

Types of data

  • Quantitative: numbers, such as mass, counts, rainfall, rand.
  • Qualitative: descriptions or categories, such as condition scores, pest present or absent, customer feedback.
  • Primary: collected on the farm.
  • Secondary: from other sources, such as weather services, market price reports or industry benchmarks.

Data quality

Good data are accurate, complete, consistent, timely and traceable to who collected them and when. Calibrate instruments and use standard procedures so data from different people and seasons can be compared.

lessons.title: Collecting, checking and using data
lessons.html:
Preparing the team

  • Explain why the data matter; people record more carefully when they see the purpose.
  • Train data collectors on methods, units and forms, with a practice run.
  • Provide calibrated instruments and check them regularly: scales with test weights, rain gauges level and clear, meters read correctly.
  • Use clear forms with fixed fields, units and space for date, location and collector's name.

Collecting

  • Follow the sampling plan exactly; do not choose "nice-looking" samples.
  • Record immediately, not from memory at the end of the day.
  • Use the agreed identifiers: block names, animal tag numbers, batch codes.
  • Note unusual events: storms, breakdowns, disease outbreaks.

Checking and capturing

  • Supervisors check forms daily for missing values, impossible numbers (such as a calf weaning mass of 2 000 kg) and inconsistent units.
  • Capture data into the system promptly; use drop-down lists and validation rules where software allows.
  • Keep original forms filed until captured data are verified.
  • Back up electronic data regularly and restrict access to authorised people.

Personal information

Data about workers, such as wages, ID numbers and health information, are personal information protected under the Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (POPIA). Collect only what is needed, store securely and share only with authorised people.

Analysing and reporting

  • Summarise with totals, averages and percentages.
  • Compare blocks, seasons, teams or treatments.
  • Use simple tables and charts to show trends.
  • Interpret carefully: consider weather and other factors before concluding that one change caused a result.
  • Report findings with recommendations to management.

Reviewing the plan

Ask whether the data answered the question. Drop data that are not used and add data that are missing. Improve forms and procedures where errors were common.

Key points

  • Start with the purpose, then define variables, methods, sampling and responsibilities.
  • Good data are accurate, complete, consistent, timely and traceable.
  • Train collectors, calibrate instruments and record immediately.
  • Check, capture, back up and protect personal information under POPIA.
  • Analyse, report and review the plan regularly.
